novelty_flags.label: Theorem 1 / project_justification
novelty_flags.one_line: The prose says it replaces Li et al.'s global reversal ordering, but no statement proves a strict implication, strict inclusion, or divergence witness against that published premise.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 1 (block-boundary)
soundness_flags.one_line: B is defined by recomputing the local-score difference under the induced density, and gamma is defined as the minimum of the same correcting gains, so the B=C equality and gamma>0 iff local correction are definition unfolds rather than an independent boundary characterization.

soundness_flags.label: ass:restricted-identifiability
soundness_flags.one_line: The cited restricted-ANM condition is Condition 19 applied across parent/conditioning configurations; this assumption instead assumes its identifiability conclusion as uniqueness of G0.

soundness_flags.label: ass:smooth-noise
soundness_flags.one_line: Hoyer et al. assume strictly positive, three-times differentiable densities in their theorem; a twice-differentiable compact-support relative-interior variant is not the cited standard condition.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: GENE uses the displayed R²/residual-independence fitness and insertion operation; Theorem 4.3 assumes that every lower-Reversal order has strictly higher fitness before concluding greedy recovery.
The paper studies scale-invariant R²-sortability, its parameter dependence, and R²-SortnRegress, rather than a residual-independence-penalized GENE insertion landscape.

The theorem assumes strictly positive densities and three-times differentiable functions including densities; it gives a differential constraint for a reverse ANM and notes compact-support exceptional constructions.

A restricted ANM requires Condition 19 for every listed parent/conditioning configuration; causal minimality plus that restricted-ANM condition yields graph identifiability. It does not name uniqueness itself as the standard assumption.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 16, Section 5.2 discussion of Theorem E.2 and Proposition E.3
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper states that fitted residuals preserve asymptotic dHSIC ordering and that sample splitting yields asymptotically valid p-values.
The paper introduces cross-HSIC with a limiting Gaussian null distribution for an i.i.d. pairwise independence problem.
The paper studies greedy permutation search on a DAG-associahedron for a sparsity/conditional-independence objective, not GENE's hybrid score.
CAM separates order search from edge selection and proves consistency for likelihood-based additive-model order estimation and pruning.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace gamma's self-referential minimum with an independently specified, computable primitive condition on f and pN, then prove it is sufficient and—if claimed necessary—derive a non-tautological observable characterization rather than re-evaluating C under another name.

Add a theorem that formally compares the new condition with Li et al.'s global reversal-monotone premise: prove strict weakening or exhibit a smooth ANM satisfying the local condition but violating Li's premise.

Correct the ANM assumption layer: state Peters et al.'s restricted-ANM/Condition-19 requirement if that theorem is used, and retag the compact C² noise regime as novel with a justification or establish an appropriate compact-support identifiability result.

Promote the bands result beyond Bonferroni/sample-splitting by proving a sharp adaptive-query or margin-dependent recovery guarantee and compare its rate or attainable margin explicitly with a named existing procedure.

recommended_next_step: Revise this angle: replace the definitional gamma boundary by an independently derived structural criterion, repair the ANM assumptions, and add a strict theorem-level comparison to Li et al. before advancing to Stage 0.
